links.outcome: Self-consistency of LLM outputs across repeated runs in DDI tasks
links.effect: Self-consistency was 31.0-74.2% in the pointwise task versus 68.8-93.6% in pairwise and listwise tasks; no model uniformly reliable.
links.quote: All models tended to have higher self-consistency in the pairwise and listwise experiments compared to the pointwise experiment (68.8-93.6% vs. 31.0-74.2%).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the capability and self-consistency of multiple large language models on drug-drug interaction identification tasks using a synthetic/clinician-designed dataset without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
